prior_adjudication.location: p. 1890 (PDF p. 1), Abstract; p. 1891 (PDF p. 2), Introduction; p. 1893 (PDF p. 4), Results
prior_adjudication.quote: Like Roelofs et al., we find evidence that the effects are modulated by state anxiety, but our effects are only marginal and we do not replicate the negative correlation between heart rate and state anxiety in the angry block.
prior_adjudication.reason: The neutral locator combines body sway and heart rate on PDF p. 4 with partial eta-squared, whereas the replication reports that "we focused on heart rate and did not include a measure of body sway" (p. 1891) and presents multiple partial-eta-squared heart-rate tests on p. 1893 (omnibus block effects with and without STAI, the block x STAI interaction, angry vs. neutral/happy contrasts, and baseline/pre-block comparisons). Because the authors conclude that lower heart rate in the angry block is supported while state-anxiety modulation is only marginal, no unique target effect can be identified and the overall "mixed" narrative cannot be assigned to an unidentified individual test.
